newsitem.title: FRANCE: French minister slams filmmakers over immigrants.
newsitem.headline: French minister slams filmmakers over immigrants.

text.p: French Justice Minister Jacques Toubon described as unacceptable on Wednesday an appeal by scores of French film directors for the public to disobey tough anti-immigration laws.
"I understand the position of certain artists and intellectuals because they are first and foremost people with human feelings who commiserate with human misery," Toubon told RTL radio.
"But their attitude is entirely unacceptable because film directors have no more right than anyone else to contravene the law, and especially, not the right to call on others to violate it," he said.

Toubon was commenting on an appeal by 59 film directors on Tuesday calling on the French to ignore and break tough anti-immigration laws and challenging authorities to bring them to trial for breaking the rules.

"We are guilty, every one of us, of putting up illegal foreign residents recently...We request being probed and put on trial," the directors said in a statement published in the daily newspaper Le Monde.

The signatories, including award-winning directors Bertrand Tavernier and Mathieu Kassowitz, were protesting at a law requiring French citizens to report the arrival and departure of foreigners staying at their home.
A French teacher was convicted earlier this month of failing to report that she had put up a friend from Zaire. The teacher argued she was not aware that her friend's documents were not in order.

"We call upon our fellow-citizens to disobey and not submit to these inhuman laws," the film directors said in their statement, one of several recent protests against a four-year-old government crackdown on illegal immigrants.

The centre-right government, facing a general election next year, has been spurred into tightening admission conditions for foreign residents by the rise of the far-right National Front which advocates sending immigrants home.
There are about five million foreign nationals in France including about a million illegal entrants, most of them from developing countries.
